scoring_notes: J-Book corpus is heavily weighted toward FY2026 RDT&E PEs (DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/Air Force RDT&E Vol I-IV/Space Force/AF Aircraft Procurement). Textron's named DoD programs are dominated by mature procurement / sustainment line items (V-22 P-40, H-1 sustainment, FLRAA EMD under PE 0203801A Aviation Modernization, LCAC procurement) and Army aviation RDT&E PEs that are not present in the v1 corpus. Per heuristic #7, NOT_FOUND in this corpus = UNVERIFIABLE (coverage gap), not negative signal. Pre-cutoff disclosures already capture the FARA (Feb 2024 Army discontinuation) and Shadow (Q1 2024 cancellation) terminations.

summary.thesis_note: TXT is a $13.7B-revenue large-cap diversified aerospace prime; only 21% of revenue is DoD. The J-Book divergence pattern (canonical for IONQ-class small-caps where 80-96% of revenue depends on a single PE) does not apply at the consolidated level. Pre-cutoff disclosures (FY23 10-K + Q1/Q2 2024 10-Qs) already captured the two visible negative program events: FARA discontinuation (Army aviation rebalance, Feb 8 2024) and Shadow program cancellation (Q1 2024 restructuring charge). The framework correctly returns no asymmetric short signal. Limitations: v1 J-Book corpus is RDT&E-heavy (FY2026 R-2 exhibits); Textron's largest DoD lines are P-40 procurement (V-22, H-1, LCAC SSC) and Army Aviation Modernization PEs that are not present, so most J-Book queries return NOT_FOUND (coverage gap). USAspending provides orthogonal verification: all major named-program revenue claims (FLRAA $3.5B, V-22 $1B+, Shadow $1.55B, SSC $1.4B, T-6 $1B, ATAC $208M) are confirmed as real past contracts.
